clue.text: Joker Returns; sounds like you'll get adult movie title there

indicators.note: returns tells us the card word is read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: a joker is a playing card

indicators.note: sounds like says the word you'll is to be heard, giving a pair of letters said the same way

parts.note: said aloud, you'll is the letter U followed by the letter L
A was the old British film certificate for adult viewing

explanation.surface: A villain makes a comeback, and the cinema poster seems to promise something X-rated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns CARD into DRAC; 'sounds like' makes 'you'll' the letters UL; A is the old adult film rating. 'there' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The vampire count's name has served as the title of countless horror films since the 1930s.

clue.text: Black Beauty, say, an unknown quantity

definitions.meaning: Black Beauty, the title horse of Anna Sewell's novel, is a black horse
a competitor whose abilities are not yet known

explanation.surface: The famous horse of fiction is something of a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a horse of dark colour, and idiomatically a contender of whom little is known.

clue.text: Where at the end Charon worked

definitions.text: Where at the end Charon worked

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or fashioned, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
at the end picks out the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The place where the ferryman of the dead plied his trade at life's end.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the river of the underworld over which the ferryman Charon carried the souls of the dead.

clue.text: Rubs me all about with what Deneuve sold in Cherbourg

indicators.note: about means all around, so the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Catherine Deneuve's character in a film shop rubs her wares all over.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film Les Parapluies de Cherbourg, Deneuve's character works in her mother's shop selling them.
explanation.definitionFit: The French film title means The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, and the shop sells rain shields.

clue.text: Cunning, Mr Rice; but that's not on

indicators.note: not on says the following letters are not to be kept in the name

parts.note: Archie Rice is the music-hall comedian in John Osborne's play The Entertainer
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A remark that the shifty comedian Mr Rice's behaviour is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' is British slang for unacceptable, but here it says to remove IE (that is) from ARCHIE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sly or knowingly mischievous, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Merciless blackmailer's showing very keen resentment about a politician

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the resentment word sits beside the politician

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
ire is sharp anger or resentment

explanation.surface: A ruthless extortioner is driven by bitterness against a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, someone who preys on others and bleeds them dry, like an extortioner, is called a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Dutch doctor's cutting edge English novel

parts.note: the van is the forefront, as in vanguard

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A Dutch doctor's leading-edge work is an English novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham, the Dutch professor who leads the hunt for the vampire in Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Chap mostly seen at about start of Revolution

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Mark is a man's name, a chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man spotted around the beginning of an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was a French revolutionary journalist murdered in his bath in 1793, early in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading radical of the early years of the French Revolution, killed by Charlotte Corday.

clue.text: Here we find Conrad's outcast lives and sets down

parts.note: is means exists or lives
lands means sets down, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: Conrad's outcast survives and comes to rest on solid ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad's novel An Outcast of the Islands sets its outcast among the islands of the Malay archipelago.

clue.text: Show turning up in narratives

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in says the run sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A show turns up in the stories told.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón, a stage show.

clue.text: Where you'll recover from abusing a herb?

indicators.note: abusing means misusing, so the letters of the two words are mistreated into a new order

explanation.surface: A clinic for people who have been taking drugs, misusing some herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for rehabilitation, it names a clinic for recovering addicts.

clue.text: Singers opposed to introduction of lengthy note

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Some singers object to a long note being brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the lowest female voice part, used of the women who sing it.

clue.text: One, we suppose, who pays attention to an opponent of 1Ac

definitions.text: One, we suppose, who pays attention
definitions.meaning: someone who listens, from the verb meaning to listen
Jonathan, the solicitor who fights the vampire count in Bram Stoker's novel

explanation.surface: A listener stands against the vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: To hark is to listen, so a listener could be called this; it is also the surname of Jonathan in Stoker's novel.

clue.text: New tears spilt for girl who got seduced

indicators.note: tears spilt are scattered, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh tears are shed over a young woman led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy is the young woman the vampire count seduces and turns in Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Storm to break violently as his character arrives at 24

indicators.note: violently means with force, so the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm breaks violently as a character arrives in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: In the novel, the vampire's ship is wrecked in a violent storm as it reaches Whitby (24 Across).
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish author whose most famous creation, the vampire count, comes ashore at Whitby.

clue.text: Characters in Algren, all of his kidney

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow contain the run we want

explanation.surface: Figures in Nelson Algren's books are all of his own sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of his kidney' plays on the idiom meaning 'of his type', but read literally it means relating to the kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical adjective for anything relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Maybe Sybil's pronouncements result from misleading persons with directions

indicators.note: misleading means leading astray, so the letters are led into another order

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Oracle-like utterances come from people who give false directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles such as the Sibyl gave replies to questions put to them.

clue.text: Author of The Wild Swan you might carelessly confuse with Oscar Wilde

definitions.meaning: Liam, the Irish writer of the short story collection The Wild Swan

definitions.text: you might carelessly confuse with Oscar Wilde
definitions.meaning: Oscar Wilde's full name included Fingal O'Flahertie Wills, nearly the same surname

explanation.surface: Two Irish writers, one with a swan, are easily mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of Irish author Liam, and near-identical to one of the middle names of Oscar Wilde.

clue.text: Aristotle's erroneous by-name in an affected ceremony

parts.note: stagy means theatrical or affected
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A mistaken nickname for Aristotle appears in a theatrical ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristotle came from Stagira and is called the Stagirite; the y spelling is a common error, hence 'erroneous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for Aristotle from his birthplace Stagira, here in a mistaken spelling.

clue.text: Cut out a chap with whom Burns's devil danced

definitions.note: a description standing in for the person the devil danced with

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Removing a man who once partnered the devil in a dance in a Burns song.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet, wrote the song 'The Deil's Awa wi' th' Exciseman'; Burns was himself an excise officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Burns song the devil dances off with a tax officer, the man who collected duty on goods.

clue.text: Where you'll see nude in act cavorting about?

definitions.text: Where you'll see nude in act cavorting about?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cavorting letters go around the nude word
cavorting means prancing around, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: bare means nude

explanation.surface: A nightclub where performers strip and dance around on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'cavorting' scrambles the act and 'about' wraps it round the nude word, while the surface pictures a striptease on a nightclub stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub entertainment of song, dance and sometimes striptease.

clue.text: Lamb's sayings, ones on record

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the ones follow the record

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral one, and A means one, as in a single thing
I is the Roman numeral one, and A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb's sayings, collected and written down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lamb is Christ, the Lamb of God, not the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: The term scholars use for sayings attributed to Jesus, called the Lamb of God.

clue.text: Caught a sailor on a river, and what he did

parts.note: got means caught, as in got the ball
OS is ordinary seaman
ea is an old and dialect word for a river

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed a sailor on a river, and he went off to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's career begins when he sets out on a life at sea, going to sea.

clue.text: Those who know a good book cover catalogues

definitions.text: Those who know a good book

parts.note: a bib covers the front of clothing
lists are catalogues

explanation.surface: Avid readers can tell a good book from its cover and from booksellers' catalogues.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'good book' is the Bible, not just any enjoyable read.
explanation.definitionFit: Students or experts on the Bible, often called the Good Book.

clue.text: "His — mate, Grumbuskin, long since had disappeared" (T. S. Eliot)

definitions.text: "His — mate, Grumbuskin, long since had disappeared" (T. S. Eliot)

parts.words: "His — mate, Grumbuskin, long since had disappeared" (T. S. Eliot)
parts.note: fill the gap in the line from Eliot's cat poem Growltiger's Last Stand with the swaggering word for a sailor's companion

explanation.surface: A line from T. S. Eliot's poem about a barge cat with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing or swaggering young man, a word used of sailors and a pirate's companion.

clue.text: At the start or turning back is where you'll find it

parts.note: in means at, as in at home or in home

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
turning back says the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Either at the beginning or on returning, here is where something is located.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the start: an introduction is where you find the beginning of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening section of a work, where its beginning is found.

clue.text: Where 1A was the least bit reserved

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount
put by means set aside or reserved

explanation.surface: The vampire was not in the least bit shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire seaside town where the vampire count lands in England in Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Draco regularly included among old style monsters

indicators.note: included among says the regular letters go inside the old style letters

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for old style, as in dates

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: The young wizard Draco is regularly lumped in with old-fashioned monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutish goblin-like creatures of Tolkien's fiction, a kind of monster.

clue.text: One to be cautious, perhaps, of Pinter's Davies

definitions.meaning: someone who takes care, read as two words
the tramp Davies in Harold Pinter's play of this name, who is offered a job looking after the house

explanation.surface: A careful man is one of the characters in a Pinter play.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in two parts it means someone taking care; it is also the job and title of Pinter's play featuring Davies.

clue.text: Chap returning a greeting to an author of the Vedas

indicators.note: returning says the chap word goes back to front

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a man
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A man returns a greeting to one of the writers of the Hindu scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu sage or seer; the Vedic hymns were revealed to such sages.

clue.text: "Instead of sitting down, I snatched my — hings, and hastened below"(Wuthering Heights)

definitions.text: "Instead of sitting down, I snatched my — hings, and hastened below"(Wuthering Heights)

parts.note: fill the gap in Lockwood's sentence from Emily Brontë's novel with the word describing his coat and hat, worn out of the house

explanation.definitionFit: The narrator grabs the things he would wear to go out of doors, his outer clothing.

clue.text: Bond's tuxedo we hear, and what Q provides him with?

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is said aloud to give a different word

parts.note: James Bond's dinner jacket is the clothing a spy wears, spy wear

explanation.surface: James Bond's dinner suit, and the gadgets the quartermaster hands over.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is the quartermaster who equips Bond with gadgets in the films.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that secretly spies on a computer user, the kind of tool a secret agent's gadget-maker might supply.
